It calls this.getObject(property) and then toString() on the result to get a string, which is passed to Integer.parseInt. There is no null check on the result of getObject, so if getObject returns null, a NullPointerException will be thrown before parseInt is called. According to the provided javadoc, parseInt only throws NumberFormatException when the string does not contain a parsable integer. The code does not perform any validation on the string before parsing, so the condition for a NumberFormatException (invalid input string) is not avoided. Other exceptions like NullPointerException are not thrown by parseInt; they are thrown by the calling code. Therefore, the only exception declared for parseInt is NumberFormatException, and it is not avoided.
answer: NumberFormatException is not avoided because there is no validation of the string before calling parseInt. The string could be non-numeric, empty, or malformed.
remark: NumberFormatException will be thrown if the string obtained from getObject(property).toString() is not a valid representation of an integer. This can happen if getObject returns an object whose toString() output is not a valid integer string, such as alphabetic characters, an empty string, or containing invalid symbols.
